items.text: WTI crude fell 0.9% to $96.24 (Oct 6), while Brent jumped 8.1% YTD on Middle East tensions, with the ECB citing ongoing inflationary pressure from the conflict. Geopolitical premium in crude creates tail-risk for credit spreads if supply shocks persist; particularly acute for refiners and leveraged energy equities with tight covenants.

Michigan sentiment expectations collapsed 10.1% in September (46.3 vs 51.5 Aug); year-ahead inflation jumped to 4.6% from 4.0%, the highest since June. September payrolls came in only 29K (vs 133K prior), a sharp cliff suggesting labor market deceleration is finally visible. This cooling labor backdrop relieves some Fed pressure but wage-pressure risk remains embedded in service-sector prices.

ISM manufacturing prices surged 6.8 points to 77.9 in September, the highest since the Iran war began, against a consensus of 72.3; ISM services prices also climbed to 74.0, hitting a four-year high. Both headline and core inflation remain sticky despite cooler growth; persistent cost pass-through suggests stagflation risk remains material for leveraged issuers without pricing power.

The ECB raised deposit facility rate to 2.50% in September, with the next meeting Oct 28–29. US 10-2 curve steepened to 51 bps (vs 46 prior) as Fed awaits evidence; mortgage rates jumped to 7.4%, pressuring housing starts (1,275K annualized, down from 1,309K). Higher-for-longer rate regime persists; mortgage refinancing wall remains a material credit risk.

ISM services PMI slipped to 54.9 in September (down 0.5 from 55.4), marking 27 consecutive months of expansion. HY OAS tightened 1 bp to 309 bps; IG OAS tightened 3 bps to 82 bps, while CCC OAS widened 27 bps to 1229 bps. Dispersion is widening—high-leverage and weak-credit stories face deteriorating spreads; call activity risk is building.

ISM manufacturing held firm at 54.5 in September, remaining in expansion for a ninth consecutive month, consistent with 2.4% annualized real GDP growth. Yet consumer sentiment crashed to 48.1 in September (4-month low) on inflation fears, and existing home sales fell to 3.98M from 4.06M. Growth narrative is bifurcated: production and orders hold, but final demand and confidence are cracking.

Consumer sentiment fell to 48.1 in September, the lowest in four months and down 15% from January 2026, as year-ahead inflation expectations jumped to 4.6%. Supplier delivery times rose to 53.2 on tariff-related delays; employment in services edged back to expansion at 50.1. Household real income erosion and negative sentiment are signaling demand contraction ahead; retailers and consumer credit face refinance and rollover risk.

themeCards.title: Middle East energy shock re-risk
themeCards.statusLine: ECB cited Middle East conflict as fueling inflationary pressures, with Brent up 8.1% YTD. Oil premium is pricing into upstream costs across manufacturing and services.
themeCards.relevance: Energy-linked inflation creates material cost pass-through risk for high-leverage borrowers with weak covenant cushions. Upstream hedging roll risk is acute if Brent stays elevated.

themeCards.title: Service-sector pricing power breakdown
themeCards.statusLine: ISM services prices hit 74.0 in September, highest since July 2022; no industries reported price decreases. Broad-based pricing is now colliding with consumer sentiment collapse.
themeCards.relevance: Service-heavy issuers (healthcare, hospitality, business services) face demand cliff if sentiment floor is broken. Negative operating leverage unwinds quickly. Refinance risk spikes if revenue growth stalls on volume decline.

themeCards.title: Consumer credit deterioration acceleration
themeCards.statusLine: Consumers reported 10% deterioration in year-ahead personal finance measures as anxiety about elevated prices intensified; year-ahead inflation expectations jumped to 4.6%. Consumer debt burden near all-time highs against eroding real wages.
themeCards.relevance: Auto, credit card, and HELOC ABS face rising delinquency risk. Servicers with subprime exposure and consumer finance lenders face downgrades; refinancing windows for ABS are closing. CDS on non-bank lenders is asymmetrically attractive.

themeCards.title: US manufacturing labor cost surge
themeCards.statusLine: New orders and employment both expanded in manufacturing (55.3 and 52.7 respectively), with prices index surging to 77.9. Strong demand into constrained labor supply is forcing wage and cost escalation.
themeCards.relevance: Cyclical manufacturers and suppliers with thin EBITDA margins face gross-margin compression. Capex intensity is rising to offset labor constraints; FCF deterioration threatens leverage covenants. Mid-market industrials are most exposed.

themeCards.title: Mortgage refinance cliff & housing demand stall
themeCards.statusLine: Mortgage rates jumped to 7.4% (Oct 8); existing home sales fell to 3.98M annualized from 4.06M. Housing starts dropped to 1,275K, signaling demand tail is cracking.
themeCards.relevance: Builders with floating-rate debt face mark-to-market pressure. MBS investors face extension risk. REIT refinance windows are slamming shut; equity-crunched balance sheets (especially non-agency mort securitizers) face margin call risk.

themeCards.title: Trade tariff transmission into input costs
themeCards.statusLine: Supplier delivery times rose to 53.2, with Miller noting tariff-related delays extending lead times. China's official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.0 in October on tariff headwinds and trade tensions. Cost absorption window is narrowing.
themeCards.relevance: Consumer discretionary and apparel-linked issuers face grosser margin pressure if tariff pass-through is blocked by demand resistance. Supply-chain de-risking capex is rising; free cash flow is under pressure.

regime.label: Late-cycle bifurcation
regime.detail: Manufacturing holds, but consumer cracking under inflation; services pricing power high, spreads compressing; refinance cliffs emerging; tariff tail-risk rising
